newsitem.title: UK: IPE oil futures little changed in low vol trade.
newsitem.headline: IPE oil futures little changed in low vol trade.

text.p: IPE Brent crude front month futures were little changed on Wednesday, as the market digested neutral overnight API data, brokers said.
By 1001 GMT, September Brent was two cents higher at $18.24 a barrel and gas oil 50 cents firmer at $163.50 a tonne, with both trading in low volume.
"I'm expecting Brent to meet resistance at $18.25," said Fenella Graham, analyst at Mees Pierson.
Brokers also pointed to a firmer Sept/Oct spread as an indication of slightly more positive sentiment on the physical market, where Dated Brent traded on Tuesday at August +10 cts."
It would be interesting to see if we can get through that resistance purely on the spread alone," Graham said.
GNI Research on Wednesday pegged strong resistance just below $18.50 per barrel, while it placed support at $18.00.

Data from the American Petroleum Institute (API) overnight showed higher-than-expected crude oil stocks for the week ending July 18, but analysts said with reformulated gasoline taken out of the equation, the API was flat.
API said gasoline stocks fell by 2.79 million barrels to 197.8 million despite both high output and imports.
London brokers said both crude and gas oil were likely to continue to trade in narrow ranges until further news on the resumption of Iraqi crude exports transpires.
"No-one wants to trade while Iraq is up in the air. We're in a very narrow trading range. The volumes say it all, " a broker said.
A U.N. spokesman on Tuesday said the approval of Iraq's aid distribution plan, which Iraq insists on before it resumes exports, was not expected until the end of July.
Iraq needs to sell around 1.5 million barrels of crude per day in order to raise the $1 billion it needs to buy humanitarian aid before the deal ends in September.
The second phase of the oil-deal started on June 8.
